pr_title: SD: Add target creation failure counter and change failure handling
pr_body:
<!--
    Don't forget!
    
    - If the PR adds or changes a behaviour or fixes a bug of an exported API it would need a unit/e2e test.
    
    - Where possible use only exported APIs for tests to simplify the review and make it as close as possible to an actual library usage.
    
    - No tests are needed for internal implementation changes.
    
    - Performance improvements would need a benchmark test to prove it.
    
    - All exposed objects should have a comment.
    
    - All comments should start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
 -->

This PR adds an error counter for target creation failures and changes the way failures are handled so that a single invalid target does not pause scraping for the entire group.

Fixes #8438

On a side note, maybe it would be better to change this counter to a gauge and have it represent the current number of failures, not just the accumulated failures over time. That might provide more useful information for remediation.
pr_comments:
> On a side note, maybe it would be better to change this counter to a gauge and have it represent the current number of failures, not just the accumulated failures over time. That might provide more useful information for remediation.

A counter is easier to implement and I expect this to simply be 0 in any setups.
If you are into mixins, would you do the mixin update in the same PR?

Never done any mixin work before, but I'll guess give it a try. Do you mean to add an alert `alerts.libsonnet`?

Edit: and also here?

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/af5a7d1078cee78856d38a879d9ce33a6fdc10b7/documentation/prometheus-mixin/dashboards.libsonnet#L53-L64

That one is scrape, not discovery.

Just an alert would do.

I changed the range to 30 minutes, which should give enough time for the alert to be noticed.

@juliusv You can ignore this I accidentally committed a package-lock.json 🤦🏻

issue_context.title: SD: Need error counter in case the creation of targets fails, and reconsider target drop strategy
issue_context.body:
**What did you do?**

Consul service discovery Job for wmi and node exporters

**What did you expect to see?**

Expected to have all targets discovered and scraped

**What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?**

Node exporters were fine but nothing in discovery page and nothing scraped for wmi
Got error in log prometheus (see log)
Only one server had a wrong IP address but the whole discovery job failed. (249 IP were OK and 1 was wrong ==> no scrape at all)

Didnt find any metrics that reflect this error, impossible to monitor
sd shouldnt discard all targets if only one is wrong

**Environment**

* System information:

	Linux 3.10.0-1127.18.2.el7.x86_64 x86_64

* Prometheus version:

	version 2.23.0

* Prometheus configuration file:
```
- job_name: 'generic-exporter-consul'
  scrape_timeout: 30s
  consul_sd_configs:
    - server: 'ipconsul:8500'
      token : 'token'
      datacenter: 'dc1'
      tag_separator: ';'
      services:
        - node-exporter
        - wmi-exporter
 
  relabel_configs:

    - source_labels: ['__meta_consul_service']
      target_label:  'job'

    - source_labels: ['__meta_consul_node']
      target_label:  'info_fqdn'
      replacement:   '$1'
```


* Logs:
```
level=error ts=2021-02-03T15:13:20.828Z caller=scrape.go:421 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=generic-exporter-consul msg="creating targets failed" err="instance 564 in group wmi-exporter: \"172.x.x.x/172.x.x.x:9182\" is not a valid hostname",
```
comments:
Thank you!

Do you have any idea why the IP address was not correct in consul? is that something actionable in our side?

If there is an error in a service discovery, IIRC prometheus should keep the old targets.

**action:** There should be metrics for this, but by looking at the code, indeed there are no metrics now. We should have a about failed targets sync.

It was a copy/paste error on app who wrote into consul, and yes we did correct it. 
The ip shouldnt have been wrong (dont know why consul allowed it) but the problem is that it froze all scrape for this "service" (wmi-exporter).
This behaviour is not normal and the fact that there is no metric to track thoses errors too.

just experience very similar error with ec2 SD, resulting in the entire job being dropped until the affected instance was terminated

level=error ts=2021-02-04T19:01:26.073Z caller=scrape.go:421 component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=jenkins msg="creating targets failed" err="instance 81 in group us-east-1: no address"

in this case we rewrite __address__ to a fqdn set in another tag on the instance, this occurs when the instance is being destroyed and persists ~ 15 minutes

For reference, this is the line in the code that should have a metric so that you can detect and alert this case more easily: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/8b215fe90725c72f570f0acfcda6c2597aa453bf/scrape/scrape.go#L421
Also, this has to be analyzed more deeply: Are we dropping targets we should better not drop in that case?

> Also, this has to be analyzed more deeply: Are we dropping targets we should better not drop in that case?

For me the problem is there : 

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/8b215fe90725c72f570f0acfcda6c2597aa453bf/scrape/target.go#L455

Shouldnt return, that drop all target of the group.
Should queue errors  in a array and continue.
Return array of errors at the end.
